title: Loomings — Choosing the Sea
source_chapter: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale — Chapter 1: Loomings
adaptation_principle: Reduce the chapter’s meditations to the concrete arc of a choice: I grow grim, decide to sea, choose my station as common sailor, accept its thumps and rewards, feel fated toward whaling, and welcome it for the whale.
action_oriented_synopsis: Ishmael grows melancholy and decides to go to sea at once. He chooses to ship as a simple sailor rather than as a passenger, officer, or cook. He accepts the indignities and orders of shipboard life as part of a universal lot. He favors being paid and the fresh forecastle air, reinforcing his plan to sail before the mast. He feels compelled by fate to make this voyage a whaling one. He welcomes the whaling voyage, driven by fascination with the great whale.

visual_safety_notes: Do not depict hypothetical or allegorical figures or scenes (e.g., Cato, archangel Gabriel, Narcissus, invisible police of the Fates); keep them in captions only.
No readable text anywhere: avoid legible signs, ship names, documents, playbills, currency markings, or labels.
Do not show specific named places as labeled objects (e.g., the Battery); use generic waterfront and room interiors.
Do not visualize the imagined ‘endless processions’ or the ‘hooded phantom like a snow hill’; keep whales and visions out of the art for this chapter.
Keep props generic to 19th-century seafaring (rigging, rope, sea chest, seabag) without introducing whaling-specific gear (e.g., harpoons) not present in the scene.
